checks.s: The memo identifies that the Calyx draft’s definition of Confidential Information is missing the independent-development exclusion.
The memo references Playbook §3.1’s requirement for five standard exclusions: public domain, prior possession, independent development, third-party lawful receipt, and compelled disclosure.
The memo rates the missing independent-development exclusion as High Risk.
The memo states that the missing independent-development exclusion requires approval from GC Priya N. Ramaswamy and VP Corporate Development Eamon J. Prescott.
The memo identifies that the Calyx draft limits Permitted Disclosees to officers, directors, and employees only.
The memo notes that the narrow definition excludes legal, financial, and accounting advisors, potential lenders, and co-investors required by Playbook §3.2.
The redline expands the Permitted Disclosees or Representatives definition to include legal, financial, and accounting advisors, potential lenders, and co-investors per Playbook §3.2.
The memo notes that Ridgeline Partners LLC (financial advisor) and/or Thorncastle Whitfield LLP (outside counsel) would be excluded under the Calyx draft’s narrow Permitted Disclosees definition.
The memo identifies the Calyx draft’s 18-month non-solicitation period in Section 8 as exceeding the Playbook §6.3 maximum of 12 months.
The memo rates the 18-month non-solicitation deviation as High Risk.
The memo identifies the Calyx draft’s $150,000 per-breach liquidated damages provision.
The memo recommends striking the liquidated damages provision in favor of an actual-damages standard per Playbook §6.3.
The memo recommends reducing the non-solicitation period from 18 months to 12 months per Playbook §6.3.
The memo recommends limiting the non-solicitation scope to personnel introduced in diligence per Playbook §6.3.
The memo identifies the Calyx draft’s 18-month standstill in Section 9 as a High Risk deviation.
The memo notes that the 18-month standstill has no fall-away provision.
The memo states that Verdantis’s preferred position under Playbook §7.1 is no standstill.
The memo states that the acceptable fallback under Playbook §7.1 is a 12-month standstill with mandatory fall-away upon a third-party definitive agreement or public auction.
The memo states that acceptance of any standstill terms requires board-level notification under the playbook authority matrix.
The memo identifies the Calyx draft’s 5-year survival period in Section 12 as a deviation from the Playbook §4.1 2-year standard and 3-year maximum.
The memo rates the 5-year survival-period deviation as Medium Risk or High Risk.
The memo recommends reducing survival to 2 years as the preferred position or 3 years as the fallback per Playbook §4.1.

The memo assigns approval for the 5-year survival deviation consistently with its risk rating: GC Priya N. Ramaswamy if Medium Risk, or GC Priya N. Ramaswamy and VP Corporate Development Eamon J. Prescott jointly if High Risk.
The memo identifies the absence of a residuals clause in the Calyx draft as a Medium Risk deviation from Playbook §4.3.
The memo recommends inserting a residuals clause permitting use of general knowledge retained in unaided memory, consistent with Playbook §4.3.
The memo identifies the Calyx draft’s 5-business-day return/destruction requirement in Section 7, with no retention carve-outs, as a Medium Risk deviation from Playbook §5.2.
The memo recommends extending the return/destruction deadline from 5 business days to 15 business days per Playbook §5.2.
The memo recommends a return/destruction carve-out for regulatory/legal holds per Playbook §5.2.
The memo recommends a return/destruction carve-out for electronically archived copies per Playbook §5.2.

The memo identifies the Calyx draft’s New York governing law and New York County Supreme Court jurisdiction as a Low Risk deviation from the preferred Delaware law and Court of Chancery under Playbook §9.1.
The memo designates the governing law/forum deviation as approvable by Associate General Counsel Lena F. Castellano.
The memo identifies the stipulated-injunction clause’s waiver of bond and requirement of no showing of irreparable harm as a High Risk deviation from Playbook §8.2.
The memo recommends revising the injunction clause to acknowledge that equitable relief is appropriate while requiring a court determination of irreparable harm per Playbook §8.2.
The memo recommends striking the bond waiver per Playbook §8.2.
The memo identifies the non-disclosure-of-discussions clause’s lack of a securities-law carve-out as a High Risk deviation from Playbook §6.1.
The memo notes that Verdantis is a Nasdaq-listed public company with ticker VRDS and has disclosure obligations under securities laws.
The memo recommends a mandatory carve-out for disclosures required under securities laws per Playbook §6.1.
The memo recommends a mandatory carve-out for disclosures required under stock-exchange rules per Playbook §6.1.
The memo recommends a mandatory carve-out for disclosures made in response to a subpoena per Playbook §6.1.
The memo recommends a mandatory carve-out for disclosures made in response to a court order per Playbook §6.1.
The memo flags that the Calyx draft’s warranty disclaimer lacks a fraud/intentional-misrepresentation savings clause and recommends adding one per Playbook §3.5.
The memo rates the warranty disclaimer deviation involving the missing fraud/intentional-misrepresentation savings clause as Low Risk.
The memo categorizes the 18-month standstill with no fall-away as High Risk.
The memo categorizes the missing securities-law carve-out as High Risk.
The memo categorizes the 18-month non-solicit with liquidated damages as High Risk, whether as one bundled item or as separately rated duration, scope, and liquidated damages components.
The memo categorizes the stipulated injunction as High Risk.
The memo categorizes the missing independent-development exclusion as High Risk.

The memo categorizes the narrow Permitted Disclosees definition limited to officers, directors, and employees, excluding external legal counsel, financial advisors, potential lenders, and co-investors, as High Risk.
The memo categorizes an item as High Risk that the playbook does not classify as High Risk.
The memo categorizes the return/destruction timeline and missing retention carve-outs as Medium Risk.
The memo categorizes the absence of a residuals clause as Medium Risk.
The memo categorizes the 5-year survival period as Medium Risk or High Risk.
The memo categorizes an item as Medium Risk that the playbook does not classify as Medium Risk, other than the 5-year survival period.
The memo categorizes governing law/forum as Low Risk.
The memo categorizes warranty disclaimer breadth involving the missing fraud/intentional-misrepresentation savings clause as Low Risk.
The memo categorizes a deviation other than governing law/forum or warranty disclaimer breadth as Low Risk.

The memo identifies and analyzes all eleven core deviations: missing independent-development exclusion; narrow Permitted Disclosees; 18-month non-solicit with liquidated damages; 18-month standstill with no fall-away; missing securities-law carve-out; stipulated injunction; 5-year survival; return/destruction timeline with missing carve-outs; no residuals clause; governing law/forum; and warranty-disclaimer breadth.

For each identified deviation, the memo states the applicable preferred, fallback, and walk-away negotiation positions from the playbook, or notes when a distinct fallback or walk-away is not applicable or not supplied by the playbook.
The redline is structured as a markup of the Calyx draft NDA (calyx-draft-nda.docx), retaining its structure and proposing changes to it.
The redline is a rewrite from or primarily based on the Verdantis standard form NDA.
The redline proposes specific language changes—insertions, deletions, or substitutions—for each of the ten identified deviations.
The memo identifies Associate General Counsel Lena F. Castellano as the approval authority for Low Risk deviations.
The memo identifies General Counsel Priya N. Ramaswamy as the approval authority for Medium Risk deviations.
The memo identifies GC Priya N. Ramaswamy and VP Corporate Development Eamon J. Prescott as the approval authorities for High Risk deviations.
The memo specifically notes that acceptance of standstill terms requires board-level notification in addition to GC Priya N. Ramaswamy and VP Corporate Development Eamon J. Prescott approval.

The memo notes that the Calyx draft describes itself as mutual but contains provisions that disproportionately favor Calyx as disclosing party, reflecting the predominantly one-way disclosure anticipated during due diligence.
The memo references Thorncastle matter number 2025-04217.
The redline references Thorncastle matter number 2025-04217.
The memo references document ID TWL-2025-04217-001.
The redline references document ID TWL-2025-04217-001.
The memo uses the project code name “Canopy” consistently throughout and does not use the target’s real name without the code name.
The redline uses the project code name “Canopy.”
The memo references July 18, 2025 as the deliverable deadline for both the redline and the issues/risk memo.
The memo references August 1, 2025 as the target NDA execution date.
The memo references August 4, 2025 as the due diligence commencement date.
The redline inserts or verifies the public-domain exclusion from Confidential Information per Playbook §3.1.
The redline inserts or verifies the prior-possession exclusion from Confidential Information per Playbook §3.1.
The redline inserts or verifies the independent-development exclusion from Confidential Information per Playbook §3.1.
The redline inserts or verifies the third-party lawful-receipt exclusion from Confidential Information per Playbook §3.1.
The redline inserts or verifies the compelled-disclosure exclusion from Confidential Information per Playbook §3.1.
The memo is addressed from Thorncastle Whitfield LLP, with Helen K. Lindquist and/or Marcus W. Cavanaugh, to the Verdantis in-house team, Priya N. Ramaswamy and Lena F. Castellano.
The memo copies Eamon J. Prescott, VP Corporate Development.
The memo is marked “Privileged and Confidential,” “Attorney-Client Privileged,” or with equivalent privilege and confidentiality language.
The memo notes that the Calyx draft covers “any Target employee contacted during diligence” and explains that this is broader than the playbook standard of “personnel introduced in diligence.”
The redline narrows the non-solicitation scope from “any Target employee contacted during diligence” to “personnel introduced in diligence” or substantially equivalent narrowing language.
The memo identifies that the Calyx draft’s standstill bars Verdantis from acquiring Target securities for 18 months.
The memo identifies that the Calyx draft’s standstill bars Verdantis from making public proposals for 18 months.

The memo explains that without a fall-away provision, Verdantis would remain restricted even if Calyx enters a definitive agreement with a third party or initiates a public auction, creating a significant competitive disadvantage.
The memo includes a clearly identified executive summary section.
The memo includes a summary risk matrix table listing all deviations and their risk ratings.
The memo includes a section discussing deal-timeline implications.
For each proposed change, the redline includes a marginal comment or inline annotation citing the relevant playbook section reference and risk rating.
